hero.tagline: Engineering innovative solutions with passion, precision...and a (busy) little touch of magic.

summary.p1: Cogar is an independent social networking platform built around the Irish language, designed to make using Irish online a normal, everyday experience.
summary.p2: Conceived as a personal project, Cogar has grown into a fully functioning social platform with over 5,100 registered users, available on both iOS and Android.
summary.p3: As the founder and sole developer, I have taken Cogar from initial concept through product design, engineering, deployment and ongoing operation. I am responsible for the entire technical lifecycle, including product architecture, UX/UI design, mobile and backend development, infrastructure, security, moderation systems, analytics and maintenance.
summary.p4: I also founded and independently manage Cogar Teicneolaíochta Ltd, the Irish company behind the platform. This extends my responsibilities beyond engineering into business strategy, commercial development, advertising, partnerships, regulatory compliance and day-to-day company operations.
summary.p5: Built primarily with React Native, Expo, TypeScript, Supabase and Cloudflare, Cogar incorporates social feeds, user and organisation profiles, private messaging, groups, events, notifications, media, content moderation and an integrated advertising platform.
summary.p6: Cogar is a practical case study in end-to-end product ownership and founder-led engineering. It demonstrates my ability to conceive and architect a complex product, make technical and commercial decisions, deliver production-ready software, and independently operate and evolve a live platform serving thousands of users. It is a modern app, done with old-school craft. I write the code myself. AI is not used on this project. This is where I scratch the coding itch.

consultancy.title: Experience, Technical Expertise and System Design
consultancy.description: Over 16 years at every level, from writing the code to running the team.
consultancy.role: Technical Expertise, Systems Design and Architecture

summary.p1: I've spent over 16 years in software, and I've worked at most levels of it: developer, team lead, engineering manager, CTO, and now founder of a live product with thousands of users. Each role shows you the same systems from a different side. That range is what I bring to a consulting engagement.
summary.p2: I've worked on the code, the architecture, the team and the budget at organisations including Web Summit, The Next Web (TNW), Picnic, Run Republic and UnitOpsMedia. That covers publishing platforms, event infrastructure, internal tools, mobile apps and the business-critical systems behind them.
summary.p3: I've been behind the scenes when things go right, and I know how much unglamorous work that takes: sensible architecture, predictable releases, monitoring that catches problems before users do, and decisions written down so the next person can follow them. I've also been there when things go wrong. Migrations run long, integrations fail at the worst moment, security gaps surface and teams get stretched too thin. Those experiences shape how I look at a system today.
summary.p4: In practice, that means reviewing your app, codebase and delivery with an eye on risk as well as opportunity. Where is the architecture holding you back? What will break first as you grow? Which shortcuts are fine to keep, and which need attention now? You get a clear picture and a prioritised plan, not a list of everything that could be better.
summary.p5: I'm as comfortable at the whiteboard as I am in the codebase. I can help shape a system from the start, review one that's already running, or work alongside your team to put the changes in place.

engineering.title: Product Engineering
engineering.description: Software engineering in the modern age — agentic, typed, and shipped.

summary.p1: I've been building software for over 16 years, including time as CTO of The Next Web (TNW). The work ran from early web platforms to iOS and Android apps used by thousands of people every day. I still think across product, platform, mobile and the systems behind them. How I build has changed.
summary.p2: The work now is agentic product engineering. React Native and Expo for the product, TypeScript end to end, and coding agents as a normal part of the build: scaffolding, refactors, tests, documentation, and the wiring between them. I set the direction, review what comes back, and own what ships. The pace comes from the tools. The judgement stays with me.
summary.p3: That shows up in the product. It is typed end to end and component-driven, tested, and released through automated pipelines — Expo Router and EAS for builds and over-the-air updates, Reanimated for fluid, native-feeling interaction, and state and data layers that stay fast as the product grows.
summary.p4: Behind the app, I own the rest of the stack: APIs and integrations, Supabase and Postgres, edge infrastructure on Cloudflare, CI/CD, monitoring and release management for the App Store and Google Play.
summary.p5: Where it suits the product, I build the intelligence in as well: LLM integrations, search over your own documents and data, and automations that connect to the tools a team already uses. Designed, evaluated and shipped to the same standard as the rest of the app.
summary.p6: That same discipline shapes how a build begins. ScopeStudio, my own AI-assisted specification tool, turns rough product ideas and client briefs into structured engineering specifications using the SCOPE framework: Situation, Capabilities, Orchestration, Permissions and Evaluation. It surfaces open questions, weighs up architecture options, risks and running costs, and produces implementation-ready build instructions for coding agents like Cursor and Claude Code. The AI proposes; nothing becomes a requirement until a person approves it.
summary.p7: Whether I'm joining a team, leading a mobile build or taking a product from idea to the stores, the aim is the same: well-engineered software that ships, performs and is a pleasure to use, built the way products are built now.

about.heading: About Me
about.p1: <brand>Busy Little Pixels</brand> is Irish Product Engineer and App Developer <link>Rónán Ó Laoire</link>. (Ronan O'Leary) Bringing years of hands-on experience building modern digital products to businesses that want to move forward.
about.p2: Ronan specialises in next-generation Product Engineering, coming from a background in web and mobile development and engineering management, delivering scalable solutions proven in production. Rónán offers the know-how and perspective of a tech lead, with the practical skills of a modern, force-multiplied developer who gets things done. In the agentic era, anyone can generate code. The edge is knowing what to build, and what's ready to ship.
about.p3: No hand-offs, no theoretical advice. Just clear thinking, sound technical decisions and quality solutions to back them up.

privacy.lead: What we collect, why, and what you can do about it. Short version: only what you send us, only to reply to you.

who.title: Who we are
who.p1: Busy Little Pixels is a sole proprietorship run by Rónán Ó Laoire, registered in Amsterdam, the Netherlands (KVK {kvk}). We are the controller of the personal data described in this policy.
who.p2: Questions about your data can be sent to <email>{address}</email>.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.form: Contact form. When you send a message we receive your name, email address and the content of your message.
collect.cookies: Cookies. We set a single cookie to remember whether you accepted or declined our cookie notice. It stores no personal information and expires after 12 months. We do not use analytics, advertising or tracking cookies.
collect.technical: Technical data. Like any website, our hosting provider may briefly log technical information such as your IP address and browser type to keep the site secure and running.

why.title: Why we use it
why.p1: We use the details you send through the contact form only to read and reply to your enquiry and, if we end up working together, to prepare a proposal or agreement. The legal basis is your consent, given when you tick the box on the form, and our legitimate interest in responding to business enquiries. We never sell your data or use it for marketing without asking.

share.title: Who we share it with
share.p1: Contact form messages are delivered to our inbox by Resend, an email delivery service that processes the message on our behalf. Resend may process data outside the European Economic Area; where it does, the transfer is covered by appropriate safeguards such as the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses. We do not share your data with anyone else unless the law requires it.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.p1: We keep enquiries for as long as needed to respond and follow up, and delete them within two years if no working relationship follows. If we do work together, related correspondence is kept for as long as Dutch tax and accounting law requires (currently seven years).

rights.title: Your rights
rights.p1: Under the GDPR you can ask us to access, correct, delete or export your personal data, object to or restrict how we use it, and withdraw your consent at any time. Withdrawing consent does not affect anything we did with your data before you withdrew it.
rights.p2: To make a request, email <email>{address}</email>. If you are unhappy with how we handle your data, you can complain to the Dutch data protection authority, the <ap>Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens</ap>.
